why: Every unvisited land cell starts a new island; flooding from it (by DFS or BFS, the source asks for both) marks the whole 4-connected component, so the count of flood starts is the island count.
hints: Scan the grid. When you find land you have not seen, what should you do with the rest of its island so you never count it again?
Flood it: visit all 4-neighbour land cells reachable from it and mark them. DFS uses a stack (or recursion), BFS uses a queue; both give the same count.
Count += 1 per flood start; mark cells visited (or overwrite with 0). O(rows * cols) time and space.
pitfalls: An empty grid ([] or [[]]) must return 0 without indexing grid[0].
Diagonal neighbours do not connect islands.
Recursive DFS on a 500x500 all-land grid overflows Python's stack; use an explicit stack or BFS.
